_comment: Migration Validator — PostgreSQL→Snowflake Transformation Rules Catalog v3.1. Single source of truth for ALL normalization rules. Aligned to the project specification: Boolean→'1'/'0', Numeric compared at full native precision (no rounding), Timestamps formatted to microsecond precision, UUID case preserved (no uppercasing), Text trimmed, NULL→'<<NULL>>', Snowflake side adds WHERE _FIVETRAN_ACTIVE=TRUE.

rules.description: PostgreSQL BOOLEAN (true/false) and Snowflake BOOLEAN (TRUE/FALSE) are both normalised to text '1' (true) or '0' (false). NULL → '<<NULL>>' via COALESCE wrapper. This avoids case differences (true vs TRUE) and ensures direct text comparison.
rules.pg_expression: CASE WHEN {col} = true THEN '1' WHEN {col} = false THEN '0' ELSE NULL END
rules.sf_expression: CASE WHEN {col} = TRUE THEN '1' WHEN {col} = FALSE THEN '0' ELSE NULL END
rules.notes: Project spec: 'Converts TRUE/FALSE to text 1 or 0. If NULL shows <<NULL>>.' Using '1'/'0' (not 'TRUE'/'FALSE') eliminates all case differences.

rules.description: Casts numeric/decimal values to text at their full native precision — no rounding. Catches real precision drift between source and target instead of hiding it. NULL → '<<NULL>>'.
rules.notes: 2dp rounding removed by team decision — full precision is now compared as-is. MONEY still gets an intermediate CAST AS NUMERIC to strip currency formatting ('$100.00' → 100.00), not to round it.

rules.description: Formats TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE to microsecond precision ('YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS.FF6' / '.US' on Postgres). Fractional seconds are compared, not stripped. NULL → '<<NULL>>'.
rules.notes: Fractional-second stripping removed by team decision — microsecond precision is now compared, matching the source_rule/target_rule sheet ('Compare till microseconds').

rules.description: Converts timezone-aware timestamps to UTC then formats to microsecond precision. Eliminates timezone offset differences while still comparing fractional seconds. NULL → '<<NULL>>'.
rules.notes: Converts to UTC first, then formats to microsecond precision — matching the source_rule/target_rule sheet ('Compare till microseconds').

rules.description: Formats DATE columns as 'YYYY-MM-DD' text for uniform comparison. DATE is consistent between PostgreSQL and Snowflake but must be converted to text for equality comparison. NULL → '<<NULL>>'.
rules.notes: Project spec: 'Formats as YYYY-MM-DD. If NULL shows <<NULL>>.'

rules.description: Trims leading and trailing whitespace from text/varchar/char columns. Empty string '' remains as '' — NOT converted to NULL (kept semantically different from NULL). NULL → '<<NULL>>'. This is also the DEFAULT FALLBACK for unrecognised type pairs.
rules.notes: Project spec: 'Trims leading and trailing spaces. Empty string remains blank (kept different from NULL). If NULL shows <<NULL>>.'

rules.description: Converts UUID to text and trims spaces. Case is NOT normalized — if source and target store UUIDs in different case, that is now a real, surfaced mismatch instead of being hidden. NULL → '<<NULL>>'.
rules.notes: UPPER() removed by team decision — case is compared as-stored. If source/target legitimately differ in case by design, revisit this rule rather than silently uppercasing again.

rules.description: Casts integer-family columns to text for cross-system comparison. PostgreSQL INTEGER is 32-bit, BIGINT is 64-bit; Snowflake NUMBER is arbitrary precision. Converting both to text string representation eliminates type-width mismatches. NULL → '<<NULL>>'.
rules.notes: Project spec: 'Converts to text. Converted to text. If NULL shows <<NULL>>.'

rules.description: Recursively flattens JSON/JSONB into sorted path=value pairs before comparison. PostgreSQL uses a recursive CTE over jsonb_each/jsonb_array_elements; Snowflake uses LATERAL FLATTEN(RECURSIVE => TRUE). Leaf values retain their datatype (number unquoted, string double-quoted, boolean as true/false, JSON null as 'null'). Object keys are sorted alphabetically at every level; array elements retain their 0-based index. SQL NULL → '<<NULL>>'; empty object {} and empty array [] are preserved as distinct sentinels. No TRIM is applied — whitespace inside JSON strings is semantically significant.
rules.pg_expression: (WITH RECURSIVE _jf(path,val) AS (SELECT k,v FROM jsonb_each({col}::jsonb) AS t(k,v) UNION ALL SELECT _jf.path||'.'||t.k,t.v FROM _jf,jsonb_each(_jf.val) AS t(k,v) WHERE jsonb_typeof(_jf.val)='object' UNION ALL SELECT _jf.path||'['||t.ord::text||']',t.v FROM _jf,jsonb_array_elements(_jf.val) WITH ORDINALITY AS t(v,ord) WHERE jsonb_typeof(_jf.val)='array') SELECT COALESCE(CASE WHEN {col} IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN {col}::jsonb='{}' THEN '{}' WHEN {col}::jsonb='[]' THEN '[]' ELSE (SELECT string_agg(path||'='||CASE jsonb_typeof(val) WHEN 'string' THEN '"'||(val#>>'{}}')||'"' WHEN 'null' THEN 'null' ELSE val::text END,'|' ORDER BY path) FROM _jf WHERE jsonb_typeof(val) NOT IN ('object','array')) END,'<<EMPTY>>'))
rules.sf_expression: (SELECT COALESCE(CASE WHEN {col} IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN {col}=PARSE_JSON('{}') THEN '{}' WHEN {col}=PARSE_JSON('[]') THEN '[]' ELSE (SELECT LISTAGG(f.path||'='||CASE WHEN IS_NULL_VALUE(f.value) THEN 'null' WHEN TYPEOF(f.value)='TEXT' THEN '"'||f.value::STRING||'"' ELSE f.value::STRING END,'|') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY f.path) FROM LATERAL FLATTEN(INPUT=>PARSE_JSON(CAST({col} AS STRING)),RECURSIVE=>TRUE) f WHERE TYPEOF(f.value) NOT IN ('OBJECT','ARRAY') OR IS_NULL_VALUE(f.value)) END,'<<EMPTY>>'))
rules.notes: Datatype-aware normalization: 22 ≠ '22', true ≠ 'true'. No TRIM on JSON values. SQL NULL, JSON null, {}, and [] are all distinct. Path format: object keys use dot-notation (a.b), array indexes use bracket-notation (a[0]).

rules.description: Converts PostgreSQL hstore to a deterministic sorted key=value string before comparison. Source uses hstore_to_jsonb() + jsonb_each() to extract and sort keys, then string_agg assembles 'key=value|key=value' pairs. Target (Snowflake VARCHAR/VARIANT, where Fivetran stores hstore as JSON) uses LATERAL FLATTEN + LISTAGG to produce the same format. Whitespace inside values is preserved — no TRIM. SQL NULL → '<<NULL>>'; empty hstore → '<<EMPTY>>'.
rules.pg_expression: (SELECT COALESCE(CASE WHEN {col} IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN {col}=''::hstore THEN '<<EMPTY>>' ELSE (SELECT string_agg(k||'='||(v#>>'{}'),'|' ORDER BY k) FROM jsonb_each(hstore_to_jsonb({col})) AS t(k,v)) END,'<<EMPTY>>'))
rules.sf_expression: (SELECT COALESCE(CASE WHEN {col} IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN TRIM(CAST({col} AS STRING)) IN ('{}','') THEN '<<EMPTY>>' ELSE (SELECT LISTAGG(f.key||'='||f.value::STRING,'|') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY f.key) FROM LATERAL FLATTEN(INPUT=>PARSE_JSON(CAST({col} AS STRING))) f) END,'<<EMPTY>>'))
rules.notes: Keys sorted alphabetically for deterministic comparison. No TRIM — whitespace in hstore values is significant. Fivetran migrates hstore as a JSON string in Snowflake; PARSE_JSON parses it back for FLATTEN. Empty hstore and empty JSON object {} both map to '<<EMPTY>>'.

rules.description: Converts binary data into a hexadecimal text representation before comparison. PostgreSQL encode(col,'hex') produces lowercase hex; Snowflake LOWER(HEX_ENCODE(col)) normalised to lowercase for consistency. NULL → '<<NULL>>'.
rules.notes: Project spec: 'Converts binary data into a hexadecimal/text representation before comparison.' Both sides normalised to lowercase hex for consistent comparison.

null_rule.description: Universal NULL handling applied to ALL columns. SQL NULL ≠ NULL (NULL comparisons always return NULL/unknown). Converting NULL to '<<NULL>>' sentinel makes comparisons work correctly. Applied as the outermost COALESCE wrapper after all other transformations.
null_rule.notes: Project spec: '<<NULL>> placeholder → SQL treats NULL ≠ NULL; converting NULL to a comparable value avoids false mismatches.' Applied to EVERY column regardless of type.

fivetran_filter.description: Snowflake-side filter added when _FIVETRAN_ACTIVE column is detected. Ensures only the LATEST active record is compared instead of historical Fivetran change-tracking snapshots.
fivetran_filter.notes: Project spec: 'WHERE _FIVETRAN_ACTIVE = TRUE — ensures only the latest active record is compared instead of historical snapshots.' Auto-detected by SnowflakeExtractor.has_fivetran_active().

rule_application_order.description: Rules applied innermost to outermost — type-specific transformation first, NULL placeholder last.
order: integer   (CAST to text — innermost for integer types)
timestamp_tz (CONVERT_TIMEZONE UTC, then format to microseconds)
